question: Should Twilio-backed RCS be a bundled OpenClaw channel, or should it ship as an independently distributed ClawHub plugin using the existing channel SDK?
rationale: The implementation is technically substantial, but repository vision favors modular service-specific capabilities and the existing bundled SMS precedent creates a genuine product-boundary exception that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Ship through ClawHub
options.body: Keep the provider-specific channel external and split out only a narrowly proven generic core API gap if the current SDK is insufficient.

options.title: Sponsor bundled RCS
options.body: Approve RCS at the same distribution tier as SMS, then require live carrier proof, dependency authorization, upgrade review, and lockfile cleanup before merge.

options.title: Keep SMS interoperability only
options.body: Retain current-main RCS address normalization in SMS and defer first-class rich RCS operation until demand or provider support justifies a separate channel.

recommendation.title: Ship through ClawHub
recommendation.body: Keep the provider-specific channel external and split out only a narrowly proven generic core API gap if the current SDK is insufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: The bundled SMS channel history provides the closest repository precedent for deciding whether its RCS successor should receive the same distribution treatment.
